transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chu (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO - Cobalt), Priya Singh (ML Eng - Cobalt), Mark Rivera (Infra Lead - Cobalt)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync to review latest benchmark results comparing Redwood POC runs vs baseline provider (CloudModel Inc.). Discussed latency/throughput numbers, tuning (batching, KV cache, quantization), infra differences (T4 vs A100), and next steps for a short dedicated test window. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics:
- Baseline provider numbers and what they measured
- Redwood POC numbers and where wins are (latency, throughput)
- Tail latency and p95/p99 behavior under load
- Cost tradeoffs (dedicated vs hosted, quantization)
- Security/operational checklist for next test window

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining uh quick roll call, we got jordan, priya, mark and ethan on our side, hi all
[00:18] Jordan: yep hey, sorry running a bit late traffic, all good now
[00:25] Ethan: no worries, we'll jump right in, maya you want to kick off with the benchmark summary?
[00:30] Maya: yeah so quick context, last week we ran the same workload against both the baseline provider, cloudmodel inc, and our dedicated POC cluster. We tried to keep model weights and tokenizer same as much as possible, used the 13B variant for parity, quantized to int8 for the baseline run to match what they offered.
[01:05] Priya: quick question on that, you said quantized to int8 on both? baseline did int8 and you did int8 too?
[01:12] Maya: baseline was int8 on their managed infra, for our runs we did both fp16 and int8 — the numbers I want to highlight are from our int8 runs since that's the closest apples-to-apples.
[01:24] Mark: and what hardware was cloudmodel on? T4s or A100s?
[01:29] Ethan: baseline cloudmodel run we got from their published benchmark — looks like they were on T4-equivalent nodes for that tier, our test cluster was an A100-backed dedicated pool for the POC, also ran a T4 replica to show parity.
[01:50] Jordan: ok good. so can you share top-line metrics? p50/p95 and throughput?
[01:55] Maya: sure — top-line: baseline (CloudModel Inc) int8 on T4: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~360ms, sustained throughput ~180 req/s for our test prompt mix. Redwood POC int8 on A100: p50 ~88ms, p95 ~230ms, sustained throughput ~260 req/s. On Redwood T4 replica (int8) we saw p50 ~130ms, p95 ~400ms, throughput ~170 req/s — so the A100 cluster is the area where we see the biggest delta.
[02:40] Priya: so roughly 40% better throughput on A100? and lower tail latency, that's promising. what's the request size? tokens per request?
[02:48] Ethan: average token gen per request about 220 tokens, prompt+response around 350 tokens total, we also did a 2k token sequence test which I'll talk about later.
[03:00] Jordan: what about batching config — were you doing dynamic batching? how big were batches?
[03:05] Maya: good call — for the production-like run we used continuous batching with a max batch size of 32, target latency SLO of 150ms for the fast path. For the A100 runs we could push batch size to 48 with minimal p50 impact, which helped throughput.
[03:23] Mark: any notes on KV cache behavior? that's been a pain point for us in production.
[03:28] Ethan: yeah we instrumented KV cache hit rates — across similar workloads Redwood's runtime kept FV cache priming and prefix caching, we saw effective hit rates of ~68% for repeated contexts which reduced per-token compute. Baseline runs had lower caching reuse because of their stateless model routing, so you'd see higher token compute per request.
[04:02] Priya: that might explain the better cost/perf. do you have absolute token/sec numbers?
[04:08] Maya: A100 int8 run: ~12.5k tokens/sec aggregate for the cluster, baseline T4 ~8.2k tokens/sec.
[04:18] Jordan: those are cluster aggregates — per-GPU?
[04:21] Ethan: per A100 roughly 2.5–3k tokens/sec depending on sequence length and batch. T4s were ~900–1,100 tokens/sec per GPU in our tests.
[04:38] Jordan: ok makes sense. what about tail p99 numbers under sustained load? that's where our users complain.
[04:45] Maya: p99 on A100 cluster was ~420ms for the int8 13B under our test mix. Baseline p99 was ~900ms under the same sustained 1 minute spike. We instrumented queuing and saw that CloudModel's autoscaling was slower which increased queueing latency.
[05:05] Mark: autoscaling slower — are they using cold-starts for model shards?
[05:10] Ethan: appears so, they had shard cold starts and longer startup times. Redwood's dedicated pool keeps warmed hot replicas and has faster routing/fallback policies so tail behavior was better. There are some noisy neighbor effects on shared tiers we called out in the notes.
[05:34] Priya: Thanks, can you say more about cost differentials? per-token or per-hour?
[05:40] Maya: baseline vendor quoted an effective cost of $0.017 per 1k tokens for their managed tier on T4. For Redwood on dedicated A100 run we estimated $0.020 per 1k tokens if fully reserved, but effective cost at our observed throughput with batching and cache drops to ~0.013 per 1k tokens. So depending on utilization, Redwood tightens up.
[06:05] Jordan: interesting that reserved A100 appears cheaper effective when utilization high. we are concerned about utilization though, our traffic is spiky.
[06:12] Ethan: that's fair, which is why we suggested a hybrid routing — hosted capacity for burst, dedicated pool for baseline traffic. Redwood supports routing policies to fall back to hosted or lower-cost instances for bursts.
[06:28] Priya: on quantization — any model quality regressions observed at int8? we care about hallucination/regression metrics
[06:34] Ethan: we ran the Redwood evaluation harness on our prompt-set; small delta in ROUGE/BLEU on a subset — basically within acceptable thresholds for the use-cases you outlined. We also included a canary with fp16 to compare; fp16 had slightly better exact-match on some entity extraction tasks but the difference wasn't large for most prompts.
[06:57] Jordan: can you include the eval results in the spreadsheet?
[07:02] Maya: absolutely, it's in the attached benchmark sheet — I'll send the updated one after the call with clearer tabs.
[07:10] Mark: infra question — for the dedicated run did you enable network egress controls / VPC peering? we need to ensure data residency and restricted egress for prod POC
[07:20] Ethan: yes the POC A100 pool was in a private VPC with VPC peering configured to your test account per last week's setup. We also validated KMS integration for in-flight encryption of model checkpoints.
[07:34] Priya: you said KMS — is that customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed?
[07:38] Maya: POC used Redwood-managed KMS for convenience but we can enable customer-managed KMS/HSM for private deployments and we have SOC2 docs; security is a separate deep-dive but we'll share the packet.
[07:55] Jordan: please share SOC2 and SAML/SSO integration docs, we typically run an internal security review.
[08:00] Maya: noted — next steps include sending those docs and proposing an SSO test.
[08:06] Ethan: going back to heavy seq len 2k test — when we pushed 2k tokens the A100 int8 p50 jumped to ~420ms, p95 ~820ms but throughput didn't drop off a cliff — it was still better than baseline T4 which hit p95 >1.6s under the same conditions. So for your long-context use-cases A100 still wins.
[08:34] Priya: that's helpful. how much did effective batching change with 2k sequences?
[08:38] Ethan: effective batch sizes dropped because of memory pressure, max batch we used was 8 for 2k sequences on A100 vs 48 for short sequences. So some of throughput advantage is reduced but still meaningful.
[08:51] Jordan: any notes about model variants — 7B vs 13B — throughput difference?
[08:57] Maya: 7B obviously faster; on A100 int8 a 7B gave p50 ~40ms and throughput ~460 req/s for the test mix. We included a 7B vs 13B sheet to show cost/perf tradeoffs.
[09:12] Mark: we might prefer 7B for chat assistants, 13B for summarization-heavy jobs. Good to have both options.
[09:19] Priya: on reliability — did you simulate region failover? we need cross-region fallback.
[09:25] Ethan: we did a routing failover test — took under 6s for routing to switch to fallback region and no data loss; there's a brief degrade in p95 while new replicas spin up but the automatic fallback gave graceful degradation. Baseline provider had slower cross-region failover in our tests.
[09:45] Jordan: excellent. anything else on the infra side?
[09:49] Maya: one note — we saw that baseline provider's published numbers didn't include KV cache reuse and had a higher cold-start variance; we've annotated that in the notes.
[09:59] Priya: can you clarify the exact prompt set used vs our prod traces?
[10:05] Ethan: prompt set was the anonymized subset you shared last week plus synthetic variations, we kept the distribution aligned to your 70/20/10 split of short/medium/long. We'll include the exact seed and samples in the sheet.
[10:20] Jordan: perfect. next, on the dedicated test window — we agreed to provision a 2-hour slot where we'll run traffic from your prod-like harness, can we get the dates?
[10:29] Maya: we propose next Tuesday 2026-03-10 morning UTC, but if that conflicts we can do Wed. Priya, Mark, Jordan can you confirm availability?
[10:38] Priya: Tue morning ok for me; Jordan?
[10:40] Jordan: Tue morning mostly good, fine from 09:00 UTC.
[10:44] Mark: same.
[10:46] Maya: great I'll send calendar invite and include the access list instructions.
[10:50] Ethan: last technical note — tuning knobs we recommend: continuous batching (adaptive), prefix/KV caching enabled, mixed precision int8 for cost, and model pinning to reduce shard cold starts during spikes. We'll put config examples in the sheet.
[11:11] Priya: for the canary we'll need guidance on rollout config, like incremental traffic percentage and rollback thresholds
[11:18] Ethan: we'll provide a canary template: start at 5% traffic for 30 minutes, check p95 & error rates against baseline, increment to 25% then 50% with health checks.
[11:31] Jordan: and who is owning the rollback? our infra or Redwood?
[11:35] Maya: typically we set automatic rollback on the platform, you (Cobalt) control the policy and can approve manual rollout, but Redwood will help configure and monitor the metrics.
[11:47] Mark: security review timeline?
[11:50] Maya: propose 2026-03-11 for vendor security review meeting; I'll attach SOC2, ISO notes, SAML integration steps, and our KMS/HSM options.
[12:03] Priya: awesome. any competitors notes? Jordan asked earlier if cloudmodel had different pricing tiers
[12:10] Maya: CloudModel sells a lower-latency A100 tier but it's significantly more expensive; FastServeAI was mentioned by your team last quarter but not part of these benchmark runs. We'll keep that in mind if you want an additional comparison.
[12:25] Jordan: good to know. let's recap actions and next steps.
[12:29] Maya: recap: I'll send benchmark spreadsheet with evals, annotated notes, and security docs by 2026-03-06. Ethan will run the extra A100 vs T4 2k token test and share logs by 2026-03-08. Priya/Jordan confirm dedicated test window on Tue 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC and provide access list by 2026-03-05. We'll schedule vendor security review for 2026-03-11. Anything else?
[12:56] Jordan: that covers it, thanks team.
[13:00] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and slack.

End of call.
